Declare a population of strata for an estimand

Source: R/population.R
pollin_population.Rd

A population made of the levels (strata) of one column of the data, for example distance bands, regions or varieties, each weighted by its area. Passed to pollin_estimand() as population, it carries the estimand from the trial to the population: within each stratum the expected response under each arm comes from the fitted model, and the population arm means are the area-weighted sums of the stratum arm means:

Usage

pollin_population(by, weights, label = NULL)

Arguments

by

Name of the column whose levels are the strata.

weights

Named numeric vector of stratum areas, one positive value per level of by, named by level. Any unit of area serves: the weights are normalised to sum to 1 and the values given are kept as area.

label

Optional short description of the population, for printing.

Value

An object of class pollin_population: a list holding by, the normalised weights, the area values as given, and label.

Details

high_pop = sum(w * high_stratum) and low_pop = sum(w * low_stratum),

with the weights w normalised to sum to 1. The estimand is formed from the two population means, so on the ratio scale the population loss share is 1 - sum(w * low_stratum) / sum(w * high_stratum): a ratio of population means, not a weighted mean of the stratum loss shares. The two agree when every stratum has the same expected response in the high arm, or the same loss share; in general they differ.

The model must be fitted with the strata as its by column, pollin_fit(estimand, by = <by>), and the population estimand is read with pollin_draws().

See also

pollin_estimand(), pollin_draws().

Examples

pollin_population(
  "Region",
  c(north = 1200, south = 800),
  label = "two growing regions"
)
#> <pollin_population>
#>   label   : two growing regions 
#>   strata  : 2 levels of Region 
#>   weights : north 0.6, south 0.4 (area, normalised)
